violations.observation: Open drinking containers used or stored in a manner that may contaminate food, food contact surfaces or utensils. Observed open drinking container belonging to employees at cook line.
violations.corrective_action: Food employees may have beverages in the kitchen areas as long as they are covered and consumed through a straw and stored in a manner that will prevent contamination to food, equipment, utensils, linens, and single service items. out_items.name: Required records available: shellstock tags, parasite destruction

violations.title: Shellstock Removed from Tagged or Labeled Container
violations.observation: Shellstock has been removed from the tagged/labeled container without preserving source identification. Observed clams and mussels removed from original container without tag.
violations.corrective_action: Shellstock that has been removed from the tagged/labeled container must have a system used to identify source. PIC photocopied original shell stock tags and placed with separated shell stock.

violations.title: Separation of Raw Animal and RTE Foods
violations.observation: Raw animal food storage, preparation, holding or display conducted in a manner that may cause cross contamination of ready-to-eat food as follows: observed raw chicken, mussels stored above produce and ready to eat foods in 2 door prep and walk in cooler.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from cross contamination by separating raw animal foods like poultry, beef, pork, seafood, and eggs from cooked foods, ready-to- eat foods, washed produce, etc during storage, preparation, holding or display. Raw foods shall be stored on shelving units BELOW or SEPARATED from all cooked foods, commercially processed foods, washed produce, leftover foods, etc. PIC relocated raw animal proteins below ready to eat foods and produce.

violations.title: Cooling from 135F to 41F, No More than 6 Hours
violations.observation: The following cooked time/temperature control for safety food(s) are not being adequately cooled from 135F to 70F within two hours and to 41F within a total of six hours. Observed marinara prepared the evening prior in 2 DR UR display at 49-55F.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety foods shall be cooled from 135F to 70F within two hours and to 41F within a total of six hours to prevent the growth of harmful bacteria. Foods that have been temperature abused are to be discarded. PIC discarded marinara sauce. EHS conducted education regarding proper cooling methods.

out_items.name: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control

violations.title: Methods to Facilitate Proper Cooling
violations.observation: The following methods used for cooling were not adequate to facilitate proper cooling: cooked pasta covered with saran wrap in walk in cooler, marinara sauce cooling in deep pans.
violations.corrective_action: Cooling hot foods shall be accomplished as follows: 1) placing the food in shallow pans; 2) separating the food into smaller or thinner portions; 3) using rapid cooling equipment; 4) stirring the food in a container placed in an ice water bath; 5) using containers that facilitate heat transfer; 6) adding ice as an ingredient; or other effective methods. Food containers placed in cooling and cold equipment to cool shall be: 1) arranged in the equipment to provide maximum heat transfer through the containers walls, and 2) loosely covered or uncovered as long as protected from contamination to facilitate heat transfer from the surface of the food. Employee removed saran wrap from pasta. EHS discussed proper cooling methods with employee and instructed on use of shallow pans.
